items.title: Build an AI Chief of Staff with Claude and Obsidian
items.guest_line: Emily Gransky · VP of Talent @ Formation Bio
items.vendor_flag: None. Practitioner showing her own build; no product being sold. Time saving ("an hour a day") is self-reported.
items.reader_fit: Yes for in-house recruiters or TA leads comfortable with Claude: a concrete, copyable pattern (watermark plus single-job agents plus reversible-only actions). Needs Obsidian/Claude setup; agencies could adapt it to their inbox and CRM.

points.claim: Each agent checks only what changed since its last run (a watermark), which cut a half-hour, token-heavy first attempt down to something runnable three times a day.
points.evidence: Watermark; first attempt about half an hour; runs 3x a day (6:30 a.m., noon, 4:00 p.m.)
points.quote: I use something called a watermark, and I just asked Claude to do a watermark, meaning I only wanted to go look for things that have changed since the last time it ran.

points.claim: The first all-in-one version was too slow and too big for the model to find signal.
points.evidence: about half an hour and a gazillion tokens
points.quote: it would take about a half an hour and a gazillion tokens to like go through and read everything

points.claim: The orchestrator triages roughly 60 daily signals into act today, watch, and quietly captured.
points.evidence: 60 signals; 3 need you today; 4 keep an eye on
points.quote: of these 60 signals, three of them need you today

points.claim: The system only takes reversible actions and never sends messages or rejects candidates.
points.evidence: Updates Obsidian only; no Slack or email sending
points.quote: I wouldn't trust it yet to look across everything and be like, let's reject that candidate or tell this person that they need to do this.

points.claim: The smallest single-purpose agent is stable and easy to debug.

items.title: How to Automate Hiring Launches (Claude + Slack)
items.guest_line: Emily Paik · Senior People Operations Manager @ Kit
items.vendor_flag: None. Practitioner build; Ashby is her ATS, not a product she sells, and Replit/Claude are build tools. Host not named in the captions.
items.reader_fit: Yes for in-house recruiters or recruiting ops on Slack plus an ATS with an API (Ashby here): a copyable launch workflow and naming convention. Needs some build help; Claude wrote the code. Agency relevance is lower.

points.claim: Role launch was a repeated manual 30 minutes across three tools and could take days to go live.
points.evidence: 30 minutes of manual busywork per role
points.quote: every time we opened a role, it was the same monotonous 30 minutes of manual busywork

points.claim: The ATS step offers three paths to match headcount planning: new opening, link to an existing pre-created opening, or job only.
points.evidence: Ashby openings pre-created in bulk for finance
points.quote: sometimes we bulk pre-create openings in Ashby ahead of time so that we can reference it with our finance team

points.claim: Channel naming is generated in code with role-type rules.
points.evidence: Engineering gets squad name; contract roles get a contract prefix; quarter from server date matched to fiscal year
points.quote: Contract roles get a contract prefix so they're immediately distinguishable in the Slack sidebar.

points.claim: The stack is small: Node.js with Slack Bolt on Replit, calling Ashby's REST API.
points.evidence: Replit always-on server; Ashby API key in Replit secrets; job create, opening create, opening add job
points.quote: Replit is hosting this as an always-on server running 24/7 waiting for Slack with the Ashby API key stored securely in Replit secrets.

items.title: Recruiting Future Round Up Live
items.guest_line: Jim Miller · VP of People and Talent @ Ashby (co-host); host Matt Alder
items.vendor_flag: Miller works for Ashby, an ATS vendor, and promotes Ashby's fraud-signal feature (he says "we sell it"); the 16% figure comes from Ashby's own system. Episode 827 guest is from Jack and Jill, discussed by the hosts.
items.reader_fit: Mixed but useful for in-house TA: the isolate-the-time pilot framing and the cohort process are practical for a UK in-house team; agencies get less. Much of it is a recap of other episodes.

points.claim: Prove AI ROI by isolating and redeploying saved time, not spreading small savings.
points.evidence: 20 workers x 2 hours a week; remove one 40-hour week
points.quote: if you can isolate one person and take them out of that group, that's the 40-hour work week, you repurpose that person somewhere else

points.claim: A cohort process builds the pool before interviews.
points.quote: we build cohorts of candidates before anyone gets put into an interview

points.claim: Vendor-reported fraud rate in software engineering applications.
points.evidence: 16% of software engineering applications flagged (Ashby's own system, last quarter)
points.quote: 16% of applications for software engineering roles we deemed fraudulent using our own system

points.claim: Review the full applicant pool after a closing date rather than first-come.
points.evidence: 100% review; first 10% unlikely to hold the best candidate
points.quote: we will review 100% of the applications after the closing date
